articles.title: Treasure hunter strikes gold with 1,000-year-old discovery linked to 'Hand of God'
articles.summary: Treasure hunter Nick Berry's gold pendant, found near Highclere Castle of "Downton Abbey" fame, may depict the "Hand of God," a Christian symbol from the Viking era.
articles.body: A metal detectorist recently unearthed a 1,000-year-old gold pendant during a treasure search — and experts believe it may represent the "Hand of God." Nick Berry, a 58-year-old father of two from Northampton, England, was recently metal detecting on farmland in Ashmansworth, a village in Hampshire, England, when he made the discovery, according to Bournemouth News and Picture Service (BNPS). The farmland is close to Highclere Castle, the 19th-century mansion best known as the filming location for the TV series "Downton Abbey." MAN SEARCHING WITH METAL DETECTOR UNEARTHS MASSIVE VIKING AGE FORTUNE, SHATTERING RECORDS Berry said the artifact was in nearly pristine condition after he brushed away the mud. "There were three of us searching, and I was in the middle," Berry told the news agency. "I got a really good signal. I dug down and looked into the hole and saw straight away the glint of gold." The hobbyist said he had a "really strange feeling and felt quite emotional" as he pulled it out of the ground. "I just stared at it. I knew straight away it was something very different and could tell it was Anglo-Saxon," he said. RARE COIN BEARING FACE OF KING WITH INFAMOUS NICKNAME UNEARTHED AFTER 1,000 YEARS "I have been metal detecting for over 30 years and have never seen anything like it. And everyone I have spoken to about it has said the same." The artifact is believed to date to the ninth or 10th century. It may have been worn as a necklace pendant by a wealthy or high-status individual, according to BNPS. Photos reveal the gleaming, hand-shaped artifact with several small indentations on its surface. "The hand has always had a strong symbolic meaning, like when you shake hands to show the other person you haven't got a weapon in your hand," Berry said. PUZZLING SOUND IN BACKYARD LEADS HOMEOWNER TO MASSIVE 1,000-YEAR-OLD TREASURE "It must have belonged to a high-status individual, like some sort of noble person, and [it] was definitely worn around the neck like a talisman." No other artifacts were found nearby, suggesting the pendant may have been accidentally dropped by its owner more than 1,000 years ago, BNPS reported. "I will never find anything like it again." Berry reported the discovery to a local finds liaison officer, and the artifact was subsequently sent to the British Museum for examination. The pendant has been declared treasure, BNPS said. articles.title: 'Azam the, Azam hain': Will the Khan factor help or haunt Akhilesh in 2027 UP elections?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: \"Azam the, Azam hain aur Azam rahenge\" (Azam was, Azam is and Azam will remain).
articles.body: NEW DELHI: "Azam the, Azam hain aur Azam rahenge" (Azam was, Azam is and Azam will remain).With that emphatic declaration, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav sought to end speculation about his equation with one of the party's tallest Muslim leaders. But the political reality surrounding Mohammad Azam Khan is far more complicated than the slogan suggests.Nine days after Akhilesh's October 22 visit to Azam at Rampur jail, the veteran leader walked out of prison with his son Abdullah Azam after the Allahabad high court granted them bail in the dual PAN card case. His freedom, however, lasted barely minutes. The Enforcement Directorate arrested him in a separate money-laundering case linked to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, and a court subsequently remanded him to 14 days' judicial custody.The dramatic turn has put Akhilesh's declaration to the test. Once among the most powerful figures in the SP, Azam remains central to the party's political calculations in Rampur and its relationship with Muslim voters. But his legal battles, the erosion of his family's electoral stronghold and the growing challenge from Asaduddin Owaisi have turned his return into a complicated political proposition.As Uttar Pradesh heads towards the 2027 assembly election, Akhilesh faces a question that goes beyond personal loyalty: can he hold on to Azam's political legacy without becoming hostage to its baggage?(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();The brief freedomAzam and Abdullah had been in custody since November 2025 following their conviction in the dual PAN card case. The Allahabad high court's order suspended their 10-year sentences and granted them bail, paving the way for their release.However, the ED had a separate case waiting. The agency arrested Azam shortly after he walked out of Rampur jail, while Abdullah was allowed to go home.The money-laundering investigation relates to alleged financial irregularities in the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur. The ED has alleged that government funds were diverted for the university's construction. Azam is the founder of the university and heads the trust that runs it. These are allegations being investigated by the agency, not findings of guilt in the present case.Speaking to reporters after his release, Azam alleged that he was being punished for being a Muslim and for establishing a university and schools. "What is there left to say? What can I say? The law has ceased to exist. Is this the punishment for being a Muslim?" he said.The following day, a special PMLA court in Ghaziabad sent him to 14 days' judicial custody. The court proceedings ensured that the brief release did not translate into a return to political activity.Akhilesh turns arrest into political battleSamajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav responded sharply to the ED action, accusing the BJP government of using cases to repeatedly send an elderly political leader to jail.In a post on X, the SP chief said: "Let today's rulers remember that thrones change when the time changes. The conspiracy being hatched against Mr Azam Khan through these cases is being watched not just by the entire country, but by the whole world."He added that repeatedly implicating an elderly man in cases and sending him to jail was "an utterly cowardly act", warning that injustice could eventually turn into a calamity for those responsible.The response was significant because it came barely nine days after Akhilesh had visited Azam in jail. That meeting had already signalled that the SP chief was unwilling to distance himself from the veteran leader despite the legal controversies surrounding him.The ED arrest has now sharpened the political messaging. For Akhilesh, the issue is no longer simply Azam's return to the party's political fold. It is also about positioning the SP against what it describes as the misuse of investigative agencies to target opposition leaders.The BJP, on the other hand, has defended the ED action, maintaining that the law applies equally to everyone.The Muslim vote and the Owaisi challengeFor the Samajwadi Party, the stakes in the Azam Khan question go well beyond the fortunes of one leader. They concern the party's hold over a crucial section of its traditional support base: Muslim voters. Muslims account for roughly 19% of Uttar Pradesh's population, making them one of the state's largest voting blocs. Their concentration in several constituencies gives them considerable electoral influence. In the 2022 assembly election, the community was a decisive factor in around 70 constituencies where Muslims formed at least 30% of the population.The 2022 results also showed how strongly the community rallied behind the SP. The party fielded 64 Muslim candidates, of whom 31 won, taking the total number of Muslim MLAs in the assembly to 36, up from 24 in 2017. The BSP fielded 88 Muslim candidates and the Congress 75, while AIMIM fielded more than 60. Yet neither the BSP nor Congress managed to elect a single Muslim MLA. The results suggested that the SP had emerged as the principal beneficiary of Muslim consolidation, even as smaller parties remained relevant in individual constituencies.Azam Khan was central to this political equation. His influence in Rampur and his standing among sections of the Muslim community gave the SP an important local and regional network. His electoral record, along with that of his wife Tazeen Fatima and son Abdullah Azam, made the family one of the most prominent Muslim political establishments in the state. His absence from active politics has therefore left a space that other political players may seek to occupy.It is this space that AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi is attempting to enter. His October 18 rally in Tanda was a reminder that the SP cannot take Muslim support for granted. Owaisi accused Akhilesh of treating Muslims as a vote bank while prioritising the Yadav community, and questioned why the SP leadership had not done more for Azam Khan. His pitch was for independent Muslim political representation, arguing that the community should produce its own MLAs and MPs rather than remain a support base for established political families.Owaisi's intervention is significant because the SP's electoral arithmetic depends not just on retaining Muslim support but also on preventing its fragmentation. The 2022 results showed the limits of smaller parties: although BSP and AIMIM fielded substantial numbers of Muslim candidates, neither managed to convert that presence into Muslim representation in the Assembly. However, even without winning seats, such parties can potentially affect the outcome in closely contested constituencies by splitting votes.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Akhilesh's October 22 visit to Azam in Rampur jail was therefore also a political signal. His declaration, "Azam they, Azam hain aur Azam rahenge" (Azam was, is and will remain), aimed to reassure the veteran leader's followers that the SP had not abandoned him. The visit came amid growing questions over whether Owaisi could use sympathy for Azam to make inroads among Muslim voters.The challenge is compounded by the SP's wider social coalition strategy. Akhilesh has sought to move beyond the traditional Muslim-Yadav combination through his PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) framework, bringing backward classes, Dalits and minorities under a broader political umbrella. But the party cannot afford to lose its Muslim support base while attempting to expand its reach among other communities.As the 2027 assembly election approaches, Akhilesh faces a delicate balancing act. He must reassure Azam's supporters that the SP continues to value the veteran leader and his political legacy, while ensuring that the party's Muslim support base does not become an opening for Owaisi or other rivals. The 2022 election demonstrated the electoral value of Muslim consolidation behind the SP. The question now is whether Akhilesh can hold that coalition together without relying too heavily on one leader or one political family.From kingmaker to political liability?To understand Akhilesh Yadav's dilemma, one must first understand the extent of Azam Khan's influence in Rampur. For decades, Khan was not just the Samajwadi Party's most powerful face in the district but the man who dominated its political landscape. He challenged the influence of Rampur's erstwhile Nawab family and gradually built a formidable political network, winning the Rampur Sadar assembly seat 10 times. His influence extended beyond his own electoral victories: his wife, Tazeen Fatima, succeeded him as MLA in a 2019 bypoll, while his son Abdullah Azam twice won the Suar assembly seat. The Azam family's political presence became so entrenched that Rampur's electoral fortunes were often seen through the prism of Khan's influence.That hold was not easily broken. In the 2022 assembly election, Azam Khan won Rampur Sadar for the 10th time despite campaigning from jail. The BJP's Akash Saxena, one of his most prominent political adversaries who had pursued several cases against Azam Khan and his family, lost that contest. But the equation changed after Khan was disqualified following his conviction in a hate speech case. In the December 2022 bypoll, Saxena defeated Azam Khan's close aide Asim Raza by around 34,000 votes, delivering the BJP its first victory in Rampur Sadar and making Saxena the first Hindu candidate to win the constituency. The result marked a significant breach in a political stronghold that Khan and his family had dominated for decades.The erosion of the Azam family's influence became more apparent in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. With Khan, his wife and son facing imprisonment, the SP fielded Maulana Mohibullah Nadvi from Rampur. The choice reportedly upset Khan's loyalists, many of whom stayed away from campaigning, exposing a growing rift between the local Azam camp and the party leadership. It was a reminder that Azam Khan's network could still matter to the SP even in his absence, but also that Akhilesh could no longer assume the family would automatically fall in line with the party's decisions.His treatment by the central agencies gives the party an opportunity to frame the issue as one of political targeting and due process. But the party will have to contend with the electoral consequences of being closely associated with a leader whose legal record has become a recurring political flashpoint.The challenge for Akhilesh is to retain the political value of the Azam network without allowing the controversies surrounding Khan and his family to define the SP's wider campaign. In Rampur, the question is no longer simply whether Azam Khan can return to politics. It is whether the political machinery he built can still deliver for the Samajwadi Party, and on whose terms.BJP's counter: 'Mafia raj' and law and orderIn 2022, UP CM Yogi Adityanath famously said: "Even Akhilesh doesn’t want Azam Khan to come out of jail because it will pose a threat to his position [chair]. The state government has nothing to do with these cases, whether they are related to Azam Khan or anyone else. It is the court that grants bail.""Under previous governments, mafias were running a parallel administration. When we took action against the land mafia who grabbed poor farmers' land for private universities and personal fiefdoms, the Samajwadi Party developed sympathy for criminals instead of the victims," he had said.The above remarks are at the core of the BJP's attack.The BJP has consistently used the Azam Khan issue to attack the Samajwadi Party's record on law and order. The party's broader political narrative has sought to associate the SP's previous tenure with alleged criminal influence and what it describes as 'mafia raj'.That gives the BJP an obvious line of attack if Akhilesh makes Azam's rehabilitation a central political theme. The ruling party can frame the SP's outreach as evidence that it has not moved away from its past.The SP, meanwhile, has to navigate the distinction between allegations, court findings and the political narrative built around them. It can point to the legal process and the need for due process, but it cannot wish away the electoral impact of the cases and convictions.The BJP's attack also puts the SP's broader coalition strategy under pressure. Akhilesh has sought to expand the party's social base beyond its traditional support groups through the PDA framework. A campaign dominated by the Azam Khan controversy could complicate that effort.Akhilesh's jail visit, his response to the ED arrest and the party's continued engagement with Azam Khan send a message to the SP's traditional supporters: the party has not abandoned a leader who played a major role in building its political presence.But the message also carries risks. The SP has to decide how much political space to give the Azam family, how prominently to project its association with them and how to prevent the issue from becoming a defining feature of its 2027 campaign.For Akhilesh, the Azam question will ultimately be about the political arithmetic as much as loyalty. He needs to reassure sections of the Muslim electorate that the SP remains attentive to their concerns, while keeping the PDA coalition broad enough to bring together backward classes, Dalits and minorities.As Uttar Pradesh moves towards 2027, Akhilesh's tightrope walk will be to retain the political value of an old ally without inheriting all the baggage that comes with him. Azam may be an asset the SP cannot easily discard, but he may also turn out to be a liability the party cannot afford to let define its next election.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Blue wave meets red flag: On cusp of big win, Democrats face internal sabotage
articles.summary: TOI Correspondent From Washington: Just when Democrats in America were beginning to entertain thoughts of a blue wave, possibly even a blue tsunami, along
articles.body: TOI Correspondent From Washington: Just when Democrats in America were beginning to entertain thoughts of a blue wave, possibly even a blue tsunami, along came Haley Stevens to remind them that nobody is quite as capable of complicating Democratic fortunes as a Democrat.In an extraordinary convulsion barely 48 hours before Tuesday's midterm elections, the Democratic Michigan congresswoman, who lost a bitter party primary (inner party election) to progressive Abdul El-Sayed, crossed the political aisle to endorse his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers, in what would be called a last minute “defection” in Indian political parlance.The immediate political damage is difficult to quantify, but the optics and the timing – coming just when many polls are showing a Republican rout – could hardly be worse for Democrats, who are trying to persuade voters that they are united and ready to take back control of Washington. Instead, one of their own has provided Republicans with a ready-made advertisement for Democratic disarray. MAGA boss Donald Trump immediately jumped on the break, praising her “bravery.”The Stevens-El-Sayed rupture had been simmering since a bitter August primary,, which El-Sayed won by less than one percent. It was not simply a case of a disappointed politician nursing wounded ambitions within the party; the two represent sharply different constituencies and political instincts, particularly over Israel and the Gaza war.Stevens, a staunch supporter of Israel, was bankrolled by the so-called “Jewish lobby.” El-Sayed, a progressive son of Egyptian immigrants, campaigned on a more critical position towards Israeli policy and US military support for Israel. The primary exposed fault lines between pro-Israel Dems and the party's vocal progressive wing, and the schism is now threatening to play out nationally, undercutting polls pointing to a big win.Stevens initially endorsed El-Sayed after losing -- albeit without much enthusiasm -- but the truce was always more a marriage of political convenience than a true reconciliation. The trigger for the final explosion was an ad by El-Sayed supporters linking U.S financial support for Israel to the rising cost of groceries. Stevens considered the advertisement antisemitic and demanded that El-Sayed disavow it. He eventually rejected the ad's contents, but the dispute had gone personal by then, with El Sayed, likely emboldened by polls showing he was leading by 10+ points, torching a planned joint church appearance with Stevens and asking her to take a walk. She walked -- over to Republican candidate Mike Rogers.Such election-eve defections being rare in America, Democratic leaders were aghast, even as Trump and his flock welcomed her. Democratic Party boss and NY Senator Chuck Schumer, who had backed Stevens during the primary, called her decision a "despicable betrayal," while furious party flacks like James Carville used gross reproductive metaphors to warn her that Republicans would use her and discard.Democratic partisans are still hoping that a NYT/Siena poll showing the party leading in all seven crucial Senate -- five of them by +5 percent –--can withstand the last minute Stephens torpedo. The numbers are unbelievable for Dems, particularly in Kansas and Texas, where they have not won a Senate seat in decades. Even allowing for polling error, the geographical breadth of the Democratic advantage suggests a national political environment hostile to Republicans.Still, the Dem are nervous, and the feeling is not entirely irrational. The party has repeatedly discovered that the electorate it sees in surveys is not necessarily the one that turns up at polling stations. Donald Trump's political career has been built, in considerable measure, on voters who are difficult for traditional polling models to capture: less politically engaged people, rural and small-town voters, working-class whites, and those who are reluctant to identify openly with MAGA and some of its nativist and racist agenda.The 2016 election remains the defining example. Hillary Clinton's 97 percent winning certainty evaporated in the industrial Midwest and boondocks America, where Trump mobilised voters who had been insufficiently represented in polling samples and turnout assumptions. Even in 2024, Dems were surprised by the extent of Trump's support among working-class voters, including sections of the electorate that had previously been part of their coalition.This is the so-called hidden Trump voter: somebody who may not be particularly enthusiastic about the Republican Party, may not even like Trump personally, but will turn up to vote Republican when sufficiently motivated. There is another complication: Midterm elections generally have a different electorate from presidential contests. Older, more habitual voters tend to dominate, while younger and less politically engaged voters are more likely to stay home. That will favour Republicans if the Democratic advantage in current surveys – captured by a range of pollsters from Nate Silver to NYT, from Emerson College to Marist University – does not translate into actual turnout.Republicans, meanwhile, have their own problems. Trump's economic message of unprecedented prosperity is difficult to reconcile with voters worried about grocery bills, tariffs and household expenses. His rallies, which many now see as entertainment, may fill arenas but they do not necessarily fill ballot boxes. The most important question on Tuesday will therefore not be whether Democrats are ahead in the polls, which they are. It will be whether their lead survives the transition from the pollster's carefully constructed likely-voter sample to the rather less predictable business of actually voting.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Why not accept Indian citizenship?': Bombay high court questions Imran Khan over SIR protest as actor's OCI status takes centre stage
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Bombay high court on Monday continued its interim relief against Centre’s Leave India Notice to actor Imran Khan Pal, 44, a US citizen and an
articles.body: MUMBAI: Bombay high court on Monday continued its interim relief against Centre’s Leave India Notice to actor Imran Khan Pal, 44, a US citizen and an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI), after he furnished a prepared undertaking and added an unconditional apology which the court sought. The central government’s Foreigner Registration Regional Officer (FRRO) had given him 2 weeks to leave India, four days after registering an FIR against Khan for unlawful assembly in Mumbai during an October 10 protest against the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls and the CEC.Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna said, “OCI card holders are not Indian citizens." They were hearing a petition Khan filed to challenge the Leave India notice as arbitrary and in violation of his right to life.“You cannot behave like an Indian citizen. You are not even remotely associated with the SIR process,’’ said the CJ orally to Khan, via his senior counsel VR Dhond, who said he was ready with the undertaking.“Right to protest is not even available to you as an OCI…” added Justice Sethna. Dhond said they are not getting into the legality of the Constitutional rights but under Article 21—right to life and liberty which is available to non-citizens, principles of natural justice do accrue.The CJ asked what was Khan doing at the protest site and how was he connected? “What for were you there? There is a complete difference between rights of an OCI card holder and a citizen of India. You will have to categorially make a statement that you have no association with the protest…”Dhond referring to pleadings in the petition said, “glad you asked. He (Khan) has no association or affiliation with those who organised the protest the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)."Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh for the FRRO tendered a compilation to the bench and argued that it was not an isolated instance and that Khan “instigated’’ people on social media.Khan has been in India since he was 2 years old, for the last 42 years, said Dhond having studied here, worked here, married and having a child in India. He should be heard, Dhond argued. The State said an FIR is registered against Khan.Dhond said but neither has the actor been summon nor called for any probe and all offences including disobedience of orders and unlawful assembly are bailable offences. The actor was passing by and was curious to see the protesters as mentioned in the petition, Dhond submitted.“I(Khan) have at the moment no film in hand. Have nothing to do with those who organised the protest. The HC can take an undertaking that I (Khan) have no part in the protest. Before I (Khan) could even reach the site there was a police bandobast…’’ Dhond submitted.The ASG questioned the veracity of Khan’s claim over how he landed at the protest spot saying “It is a misleading statement. That out of curiosity he went there to check…He is part of the protest."Singh said the actor is a US citizen and the Centre is within its power to expel him. The Centre “requires no foundational basis to expel a foreigner from the India,’’ said Singh.“Hence there is no question of granting any protection. He takes all benefit as citizen of US and as your lordship just said Article 19 doesn’t apply to OCI. The (FRRO) has taken a decision to remove a foreigner. It is the Centre’s discretion. A visa too doesn’t mean a foreigner has all the rights to enter India.”“If you read the petition the impression given is that…he was curious… but see he has given an interview…” Singh submitted. The HC sought a reply from the Centre. “It is better that you (Centre) respond. Khan will have a chance to file a rejoinder. We can then decide the matter," said the bench.The bench remarked, “This case is purely distinguisshable…He has on his OCI registration said he is “unemployed."The Judges said to Khan, “Why don’t you accept India citizenship. You work and live here. You make films here. You are a celebrity. Why don’t you apply for Indian citizenship…You have to give a categorical undertaking that you will not participate in any such protest as you are an OCI and these are not available to OCI card holders."Dhond tendered the undertaking and the Chief Justice said, “If this kind of undertaking comes, you have to tender one with an unconditional apology…You (Khan) have everything and recognition pan India. Your (Khan’s) one statement would have decisive impact (on fans)."The CJ Tripathi and Justice Sethna orally said, “It is least expected. You (Khan) are a responsible person. Literate and highly educated. you come from a responsible family. You have a great following. Since childhood you are in India. And the country has never raised such an issue against you in the past…you cannot behave or be placed on par with Indian citizens…’’ The bench on seeing the Centre’s compilation said, “You cannot say, ‘I was a novice and had no idea."Dhond sought a copy of the compilation, saying they cannot tender fresh material across the bar.The CJ said, “Inadvertently if you had participated then there should be regret on oath. You (Khan) had no role at all in the SIR. Whatever statement you have made. You should make an unconditional apology. We will record in the order."The ASG said, “This undertaking and apology is by a foreigner as an OCI holder falls within definition of a foreigner. This is not merely a question of participation in a protestThe CJ at one point said smilingly, Khan has lived here for so long that he “forgot that perhaps you are an OCI". Power of govt to expel a foreigner is absolute court has heldThe ASG Singh said, "A foreigner has no right to stay in India Or remain in India."OCI card holder doesn’t alter the situation"OCI card holder is not a citizen of India." The bench orally said to the ASG "That the Centre has unfettered power (to remove a foreigner) we agree. But this is a case of a dispute..." and the CJ said "Vasudeva Kutumbakam and smiling said once apology is tendered perhaps the Centre would be "magnanimous".HC CJ recorded that Khan has tendered an unconditional apology and posting the matter to December 7 at 3pm said in the end to Khan’s counsel, "you must tell your clientthat filing an apology doesn’t mean it is a green signal to say or do anything...You can go to the USA and cast your vote and participate in protests there... It is a very serious matter."Imran Khan’s legal team also comprised Kunal Vajani, Zulfiquar Memon, Parvez Memon and Chirag Naik.Imran Khan’s petition against 'Leave India' notice: Key exchange in the hearingASG Anil Singh (for FRRO):Even without foundational facts, the Centre can tell him (Khan, as a foreigner) to leave India, even if there is a valid visa.The Centre has an unfettered right and facts are not needed. That’s a different thing.Khan is a foreigner, a US citizen. An OCI, not an Indian citizen.The Centre has unfettered power (under the Immigration and Foreigners Act).HC bench of CJ Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna:That you have unfettered power we agree. But LIN was issued under these circumstances (of being present at a protest). If these circumstances go, your outcome or actions could be different.He (Khan) has been here for many years. Since childhood. We have to follow Vasudev kutumbakam.Someday you may say this man must remain in India.Once he tenders an apology, magnanimity may be shown.OCI are at the mercy of the sovereign county. They have no right at all to stay here and criticise the country and its policies.Bench to Khan’s senior counsel VR Dhond:You must tell your client. By filing an apology doesn’t mean a green signal.Dhond:Hopefully his apology and undertaking will persuade the FRRO to take a different view.Imran Khan’s undertaking through his advocates, MZM Legal:I had no intent, as can be seen from my limited remarks to the media on 10.10.2026. I have never made any demands and have categorically stated that I am no one to make any demands. I was present there to see why the freedom of movement was being restricted and why people’s voices were being oppressed and suppressed.I have utmost love and respect for this great nation. I have, to a great extent and in my limited personal capacity, contributed substantially through the furnishing of taxes and the creation of jobs for several persons.There will be no participation by me in any protests in the future.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Indian-origin woman Srishti Tarana Sharma charged in US over pro-Palestine intimidation campaign at Michigan university
articles.summary: Srishti Tarana Sharma, an Indian-origin woman, is charged in a federal investigation linked to intimidation and vandalism against Jewish organizations at the University of Michigan. Learn more about the threats and escalating tensions.
articles.body: An Indian-origin woman, Srishti Tarana Sharma, 23, is among four additional people charged in a federal investigation into alleged threats, vandalism and intimidation targeting Jewish organisations, University of Michigan officials and businesses perceived to have links to Israel.US Attorney Jerome F Gorgon Jr announced the new charges, taking the total number of defendants indicted in the case to 12. The other newly charged individuals are Henry David MacKeen-Shapiro, 23, Aaron Hunter Vonbargen, 25, and Joseph Mark Fisher, 23.According to the US Attorney's Office, two of the newly charged defendants, MacKeen-Shapiro and Vonbargen, were arrested last week and are due to make their initial court appearances. The remaining two, including Sharma, are still at large.The investigation centres on alleged conspiracies to intimidate the Jewish Federation of Detroit, University of Michigan leadership and law enforcement personnel, as well as businesses considered to have connections with Israel.As per the superseding indictment, the defendants and other alleged co-conspirators developed plans to pressure the university and private-sector organisations into cutting any perceived ties with Israel following the October 2023 Hamas attacks.Prosecutors allege that the group threatened further retaliation and escalating criminal activity if its demands were not met. The indictment also claims that members used encrypted messaging services, social media platforms and overseas collaboration tools to identify targets and coordinate their activities.The alleged incidents included spray-painting threats, smashing windows and throwing glass jars containing noxious chemicals into family homes. Investigators also allege that the suspects marked homes and workplaces with symbols associated with Hamas, including red handprints and inverted red triangles.The indictment further alleges that photographs of the incidents were subsequently shared on social media alongside additional threats. Prosecutors say the posts were intended to intimidate the immediate victims and send a warning to other members of the community who support Israel.Those allegedly targeted included the Jewish Federation of Detroit, two University of Michigan regents, other university officials, a university police lieutenant, a student and two businesses perceived to have links to Israel.Commenting on the latest charges, Gorgon said the alleged threats against Jewish communities and public officials were part of a wider pattern of intimidation.“These alleged attempts to terrorize our Jewish community and government officials are nothing new,” he said.FBI Detroit Special Agent in Charge Jennifer Runyan said the additional charges reflected the work of federal investigators and several local, state and federal agencies involved in the case.“Those who believe they can threaten families, hide behind a group, and avoid accountability should think again. Justice will find you,” Runyan said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Shania Twain to headline Blenheim Palace Festival in 2027
articles.summary: The country-pop icon will bring her hits to the Unesco World Heritage site next summer.
articles.body:
Country music star Shania Twain has been announced as one of the headline acts for next summer's Blenheim Palace Festival.

The five-time Grammy award winning singer, best known for her hit Man! I Feel Like a Woman!, will bring her 2027 to the Unesco World Heritage site in Oxfordshire on 29 June 2027.

It comes after the festival, held in the grounds of the palace, announced Alex Warren as its first headliner for next year's run of shows last month.

Heather Carter, the palace's managing director of visitor attractions, said it "couldn't be more excited to welcome the Queen of Country Pop to our Great Court".

"Shania Twain's songs have been the soundtrack to so many lives and hearing them ring out in front of the Palace on a summer evening will be truly magical," she said.

The festival is organised by live music promoters Cuffe & Taylor, whose co-founder Peter Taylor said: "Shania Twain at Blenheim Palace, it really does not get any better than that."

The concert follows the release of Little Miss Twain – The Places I'll Go, the deluxe edition of Twain's seventh studio album, earlier this year.

Tickets for Shania Twain at Blenheim Palace are available on pre-sale from 10:00 GMT on Wednesday, with general sale taking place at the same time on Friday.

Twain is the third artist to be announced for this year's festival after Alex Warren and David Gray.

Warren, who is performing on 27 June, is best known for his smash-hit single Ordinary, which became one of the biggest songs of 2025 and topped the UK charts for 13 weeks.

Meanwhile, singer-songwriter Gray will bring melodies - including those from his 2000s chart-topping album White Ladder - to the palace on 3 July 2027.

articles.title: As Islamophobia ramps up in US midterms, Texas Muslims eye local stakes
articles.summary: Texas Muslims grapple with a slate of policies they say stigmatise their community, push for change at the ballot box.
articles.body:
Houston, Texas – The final stretch of the United States midterm elections has been shrouded in growing Islamophobia , centred most prominently on Muslim candidates, such as Michigan Democratic Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed.

This climate of prejudice may be presenting as a national issue, but it has been years in the making in Texas, where state politicians have pushed rhetoric and policies that Muslim voters say stigmatise their very existence.

Even without a Muslim candidate on a statewide ballot, the election’s stakes, Muslim voters said, are extremely local.

“Honestly, I feel it most through my kids,” said Samir Nadjam, a lawyer from Houston, who attended a “Fall Fest” celebration at a local Islamic centre with his family just days before the November 3 vote .

“As adults we can pick and choose who we associate with,” the 45-year-old said. “But kids, they all go to school together and you’ll have certain families who watch certain news. And kids will say things, just off-putting things.”

Muslims account for less than two percent of Texas’s population, but community organisers hope a major increase in voter turnout could flex electoral muscle. Regardless of party, many Muslim voters told Al Jazeera they wanted to send a message that they are not to be treated as anyone’s political boogeyman.

“Muslims are pushed out. They are discriminated [against] everywhere,” said Emran Gazi, the president of the Islamic Society of Greater Houston, which oversees more than 30 mosques in the sprawling metropolis.

The society vastly expanded voter registration drives this year, with religious leaders pushing the message during Friday prayers. The ISGH does not endorse specific candidates, Gazi said, but instead urges members to vote their conscience.

“We want to make sure the politicians and officials understand that Muslims need to be factored before they make any decision against Muslims,” he said.

Several voters said it was not hard to understand the grim rationale of “othering” another group for political gain. But the verve with which the rhetoric and policy have escalated in the Republican-dominated state has been staggering.

“Honestly, it’s been hell,” said Mariam Ahmed, a 42-year-old physician. “It’s got to a point where, within the last two years, I contemplated leaving the US in general.”

“I have a child. I don’t want him to be viewed as a terrorist,” added Ahmed. “I’ve already had to deal with that. I don’t want that to happen to my kid.”

The messaging from Republican Governor Greg Abbott and the state Republican party has coalesced around the concept that ‘Sharia’ – an amorphous term for Islamic customs and practices, which some countries have codified into their governments – poses an imminent threat to the people of Texas.

“We are not waiting on Washington, DC,” Abbott said at the Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas last month. “We will fully ban Sharia Law in Texas.”

Senator Ted Cruz, speaking at the same event, echoed the sentiment, saying “Sharia law is fundamentally inconsistent with the Constitution and we need to stand together and stop it now.”

In June, the state Republican party adopted an official platform dubbed “Don’t Sharia my Texas”, vowing “criminal punishment; disqualification for public, military, and law enforcement service; denaturalisation; and deportment” for any of its proponents.

Texas state legislators launched the “Sharia-free Texas Caucus” in March, which has since gained 38 members in the 150-seat chamber. That came just months after two US Representatives from Texas, Chip Roy and Keith Self, launched the “Sharia-Free America Caucus” in Congress, which has grown to 68 members.

Rights advocates and residents said the emphasis on Islamic law has been as baffling as it has been disconcerting. No jurisdiction in Texas, or the US for that matter, has enacted any form of Islamic law.

“In real life, nobody’s hating on everyone as much as they’re making it seem to be,” said Sarah Dabbas, a 33-year-old physician who recently moved to Houston. “And never in the history of the United States has anyone imposed anything like Muslim law on the government.”

“We can’t do that,” she added. “It’s just how we practice.”

Monitors say state officials have distorted a handful of unique cases, including investigating a company that sought to develop a Muslim-centred housing development in North Texas and groups that oversee voluntary Islamic arbitration, similar to practices in Christianity and Judaism.

The Bridge Initiative, a Georgetown University-based Islamophobia tracker, has said state politicians have increasingly pointed to “ordinary expressions of Muslim civic life” in arguing that Islamic law is encroaching.

That includes “public participation, demographic growth … and involvement in community development,” the group wrote in a report published in February. “In effect, they frame Muslims’ engagement as active citizens, and at times their mere existence, as evidence of a broader threat.”

The political climate has not spared prominent Republican Muslims in Texas, with the situation coming to a head in June during the Republican Party of Texas Convention.

In one instance, outgoing Republican Party chair Abraham George told two Muslim delegates they should leave the party, the Texas Tribune reported . In another instance, a state senator told a panel that Muslims were “required by Sharia to lie” to fly below the radar.

Those targeted with harassment included the son of party delegate Tarek Hussein, who founded the Council on American–Islamic Relations (CAIR) Houston office in the early 2000s.

Governor Abbott, who faces an upstart challenge from Democrat Gina Hinojosa, has sought to designate CAIR Texas as a “foreign terrorist organisation”, a label typically applied by the federal government.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who is running in a tight Senate race against Democrat James Talarico, has since sued CAIR, seeking to force it to stop operating in the state. CAIR Texas has, in turn, sued Abbott on constitutional grounds of freedom of speech and expression.

Speaking to Al Jazeera, a Muslim Republican who attended the event described the experience as “very hurtful”.

“I have been involved with Republicans for a long time,” said the attendee, who asked that his name not be used for fear of further harassment. “I identify with their business values, family values.”

While still involved in local Republican politics, he said he will leave some Republican candidates off his ballot.

Other conservative Muslims, he said, “may not vote outside the Republican Party, but they might skip voting for some of the candidates”.

Local organisers said it has been difficult to translate community dismay into statewide political action.

Sania Rahim, who works with the Coalition for Peace, Relief, and Equity, pointed to the vast diversity of Muslims in both Houston and the wider state, with no one ethnicity dominant.

“You can’t just go on an Arabic radio station and tell people about voting, because a large percentage of people don’t speak Arabic,” she said.

Muslim voters in the area have been typically more engaged in local politics than in statewide races, she said.

Still, the Texas Board of Education’s recent approval of a high school curriculum that critics say focuses disproportionately on the concept of “radical Islam”, as well as a misportrayal of the prophet Muhammad, has been a particularly energising issue.

Manning a CAIR Action table at the Islamic centre’s “Fall Fest” in Houston, Sameeha Rizvi, the organisation’s civic engagement organiser, grimaced as she recounted the difficulties of overcoming what she called the “model immigrant” mindset.

“I think the issue that we’re seeing right now is a lot of our leaders think that the best way to move past what is happening to us is putting your head down and staying quiet,” she said. “They may be telling people to vote, but they’re not speaking out in the court of public opinion about a lot of these issues.”

Picking up a microphone, she strained her voice over the din of bounce houses, petting zoos and food vendors.

“Raise your hand if you’ve voted yet,” she said. “Raise your hand if you’re registered to vote and haven’t voted yet.”

“The way we can change things, the way we can make this a safe state for our families, is by voting in this election,” Rizvi said. “There is a clear choice.”

articles.title: Arab parties back Eisenkot: What’s the latest in Israel’s coalition talks?
articles.summary: Political wrangling is still ongoing as all blocs weigh potential paths to power.
articles.body:
Israel’s Arab parties, which won a record-breaking 19 seats in last week’s general elections, are set to back opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc, further trampling Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s chances of leading another government.

The main Jewish opposition bloc, which includes four parties, fell short of the 61 seats needed to form a majority in the Knesset, Israel’s parliament, but joining forces with the two main groups that represent Palestinian citizens of Israel could help avoid a political deadlock and another election.

Already, the “Change” opposition bloc has pledged not to join forces with Netanyahu, citing security failures that led to the October 7 Hamas attacks and an ongoing corruption trial that the prime minister faces.

But taking support from the Arab parties — whether as part of the ruling coalition or as outside support — also poses a challenge for Eisenkot from the right, at a time when leaders and parties, including Netanyahu, have been openly deploying anti-Arab racism to woo Jewish voters.

Israel’s minority Arab population has long been marginalised in politics. Since October 7, however, they have been sidelined even more. At least two former Palestinian legislators, and one current member of the Knesset, have been arrested briefly for comments or acts deemed critical of Israel’s genocide in Gaza and its occupation of the West Bank.

As the parties weigh possible paths to power, it’s likely they’ll have to make compromises and break promises made to their supporters, analysts say.

A coalition of Jewish conservative and far-right parties led by Prime Minister Netanyahu’s Likud won 53 seats in a Knesset of 120 seats, falling short of a majority.

The opposition bloc, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot of the Yashar party, won 48 seats — even further away from a majority.

Meanwhile, the Arab-led Joint List and Ra’am won more seats than ever after Arab voters doubled their turnout to about 80 percent. Ra’am, led by Mansour Abbas, won eight seats, while the Joint List, led by Yousef Jabareen, won 11.

While the Arab bloc has been open to working with the opposition, there were speculations that Eisenkot would refuse their support to avoid backlash from the wider Jewish Israeli public. Arabs make up a fifth of the population of Israel. Only one Arab party, Ra’am, has successfully joined a governing coalition – in 2021. That government lasted less than two years.

Eisenkot and other opposition leaders had earlier said they would not form a coalition with Arab parties to appeal to their supporters.

Netanyahu has claimed repeatedly and without proof that Arab parties committed fraud during the elections with foreign backing.

The prime minister and his Likud party have cited a handful of cases, like the arrests of three political activists who allegedly bribed voters before polls opened. They are suspected of connections with the Ra’am party, although the party denies involvement.

Netanyahu’s case, however, appears to be weakening. On Sunday, an Israeli court released one of the suspects, and another was ordered to remain in house arrest.

Israeli election officials have also said the vote would not be undermined. Videos on Sunday of Israel’s elections chief sitting with Israel’s attorney general and the head of the Shin Bet intelligence service appeared to send the message that the agencies are cooperating to make the vote stand.

“Our position is that even if the suspicions are substantiated, this would not undermine the integrity of the electoral process or the election results as a whole,” Central Elections Committee head Noam Sohlberg said in the clip.

Netanyahu and Likud also suggested that the opposition bloc joining with Arab parties would be treasonous. In a statement after the vote, Likud warned that Zionist parties cooperating with the Arab bloc would be “dangerous to Israel”.

Some Israelis agree. Late on Sunday, dozens gathered outside Eisenkot’s home to protest a potential alliance.

Yes. According to several media reports, Joint List and Ra’am said they’ll collaborate with the opposition bloc to push Netanyahu out but not necessarily to form a government.

Abbas of Ra’am has long said he’d join a potential Eisenkot government if his party is given the internal security portfolio. That his deputy is a Jewish lawmaker is also seen as a signal to the opposition bloc.

Jabareen of the Joint List, meanwhile, said in a Monday interview with The Guardian that his party was ready to cooperate with the “Change” bloc to get rid of Netanyahu and other extremist members of the government, including National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich.

He clarified that the party has no intention of joining an Eisenkot government but that it would vote with it in the Knesset. That would allow Eisenkot to form a “minority government” with fewer than 61 seats.

But it’s unclear what Eisenkot and his partners will do next. The opposition bloc earlier placed conditions on any coalition with the Arab parties, saying they must accept Israel as a Jewish state, back army conscription and denounce Hamas as a terror group.

“The conditions that [Eisenkot] speaks of are more relevant for parties who would be in the coalition. We are not planning to be in the coalition … for very clear reasons,” Jabareen told The Guardian, adding that “as long as the occupation of our people in the West Bank continues, we cannot be part of a government”.

The election results will be certified on Wednesday.

Afterwards, President Isaac Herzog will begin meeting with leaders of the 11 parties elected to parliament to know who they want as the next prime minister. The meeting at his residence will be livestreamed.

He will then choose the candidate he thinks is most likely to form a coalition government. As the leaders of the two main blocs, that will likely be Netanyahu or Eisenkot.

With Arab parties now expected to name Eisenkot as their preferred partner, the opposition leader could be the frontrunner to get the nod from Herzog.

Eisenkot or Netanyahu will be given 28 days to form a coalition. If that fails, the negotiation period can be extended by 14 days, after which Herzog might ask another candidate to try again.

Although chances are slim, it is still possible that Netanyahu and the opposition bloc could enter talks and agree to form a unity government. Or Netanyahu could attempt to pull at least eight members of the opposition bloc.

Already, Yashar claimed in an X post on Saturday that several of its members had gotten calls from Likud, which it said was in a state of “hysteria”.

Meanwhile, parliamentarians will be sworn in on November 10 regardless of the coalition talks.

articles.title: Conservative Jewish activist vows not to be silenced after being attacked on University of Michigan campus
articles.summary: Lizzy Benichou describes the moment a woman lunged at her during an open debate on Iran and women's freedoms at the University of Michigan campus.
articles.body: A conservative Jewish activist who was shoved to the ground during a debate at the University of Michigan is speaking out about the violent encounter, vowing not to let the attack silence her. "It will definitely not dissuade me," Lizzy Benichou told "Fox & Friends" on Monday. Benichou said she was hosting an open debate on the Ann Arbor campus when a woman approached the group, began shouting and allegedly struck another conservative influencer in the face with her phone before turning on her. 30% OF COLLEGE STUDENTS SAY VIOLENCE ACCEPTABLE WAY TO STOP SPEAKERS ON CAMPUSES, SURVEY FINDS "She slapped Joe [Redden] in the face with her phone. Then she came up towards me and I told her, 'You would not be able to do this in Iran,'" Benichou said, recounting the incident. She explained that she was referring to freedom of speech, pointing to the Iranian government's treatment of protesters. The confrontation escalated as Benichou and fellow conservative influencer Cam Higby challenged the woman over women's freedoms in Iran. "I think [Higby] said, 'She wouldn't be allowed to be dressed like this,'" she continued. And there were some Jordanian students next to me, and I asked them, 'Am I right?' And then she just lunged." Benichou described feeling sore after suffering a "hard fall" during the incident Sunday. In a statement to Fox News Digital, the University of Michigan Police Department confirmed that a student was taken into custody, processed and released, adding that the case "will be forwarded to the Washtenaw County Prosecutor’s Office for review." The incident will be forwarded to the Washtenaw County Prosecutor’s Office for review. The victim, who is not affiliated with the university, was later medically treated and released. The confrontation comes as Michigan's closely watched Senate race brings political and cultural divisions into sharper focus ahead of the midterms. articles.title: Al Jazeera condemns Israeli ban extension, calls for its immediate lifting
articles.summary: Network calls move ‘assault’ on press freedom, warns of ‘dangerous pattern’ that undermines ability to report facts.
articles.body:
Al Jazeera Media Network has strongly condemned the Israeli authorities’ decision to extend a ban on its operations in Israel for another 90 days, including the suspension of its broadcasts, the closure of its offices and the restriction of access to its websites and digital platforms.

In a statement on Monday, the Qatar-based network said it considered the move “an assault” on press freedom and the public’s right to information, warning it set “a dangerous pattern that undermines the ability of news organisations to report the facts and hold those in power to account”.

It came after a court in Tel Aviv approved last week the Israeli government’s decision to extend the ban for a further 90 days.⁣

In May 2024 , at the height of Israel’s genocidal war against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s cabinet had voted to shut Al Jazeera’s operations in Israel. The decision, which was strongly criticised by press freedom groups, followed the passage of a law by the Israeli parliament that allowed the temporary closure of foreign broadcasters considered to be a “threat to national security”.

In September that year, Israeli forces also stormed Al Jazeera’s offices in Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank, confiscating equipment and documents and closing the network’s office.

Al Jazeera, which on Sunday marked its 30th anniversary, said in the statement it “categorically rejects the allegations used to justify the ban” and called for its immediate lifting.

“The Network notes that the extension was based on secret material which neither the Network nor its lawyers were permitted to see or respond to, denying it any genuine opportunity to defend itself and falling short of the most basic guarantees of due process,” it said.

Al Jazeera has been targeted by Israel for years. In 2017, Netanyahu, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court on charges of war crimes in Gaza, threatened to shut down its Jerusalem office, and an Israeli missile destroyed the building housing its office in Gaza in 2021.

Many Al Jazeera journalists were among more than 200 Palestinian journalists killed by Israel during its genocidal war on Gaza. In several cases, their family members were also killed.

In May 2022, Al Jazeera journalist Shireen Abu Akleh was shot dead by Israeli soldiers in the occupied West Bank. Israel initially denied responsibility, but later admitted there was a “high possibility” that one of its soldiers had killed the journalist, known for her ground reporting from the occupied Palestinian territory.

In its statement, Al Jazeera said that “attempts to silence it will not deter it from fulfilling its mission and continuing its coverage with accuracy and integrity from its bureaus around the world”.

“The Network is reviewing the decision with its legal counsel and reserves the right to pursue all appropriate legal measures to protect its journalists, its rights and the public’s right to information,” it added.
